original_question: For a one-dimensional unimodular Pisot inflation tiling with scaling factor λ, if the first rational Čech cohomology group has rank equal to the algebraic degree of λ, must the tiling have pure point spectrum?
target_in_paper: Section 2.2, Conjecture 2.2.2 (Homological Pisot Conjecture), stated as a topological-conjugacy-motivated refinement of the Pisot Substitution Conjecture. ([armj.math.stonybrook.edu](https://armj.math.stonybrook.edu/pdf-Springer-final/016-0046.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the exact core implication of Conjecture 2.2.2: one-dimensional + unimodular + Pisot inflation tiling + first rational Čech cohomology rank equal to the algebraic degree of λ + conclusion of pure point spectrum. In substance, that is the Homological Pisot Conjecture as stated in the paper. ([armj.math.stonybrook.edu](https://armj.math.stonybrook.edu/pdf-Springer-final/016-0046.pdf))
missing_details: The paper states this as a universal conjectural implication, so a fully stand-alone version should make the quantifier explicit: for every one-dimensional unimodular Pisot inflation tiling of the stated kind. ([armj.math.stonybrook.edu](https://armj.math.stonybrook.edu/pdf-Springer-final/016-0046.pdf))

The nearby context identifies the relevant spectrum as the pure point dynamical spectrum of the associated tiling dynamical system, so 'pure point spectrum' should be attached to that dynamical object rather than left informal. ([armj.math.stonybrook.edu](https://armj.math.stonybrook.edu/pdf-Springer-final/016-0046.pdf))

To be stand-alone, the Pisot hypothesis on λ should be spelled out as in the surrounding paragraph: λ is a real algebraic integer greater than 1 whose conjugates are all strictly smaller than 1 in modulus. ([armj.math.stonybrook.edu](https://armj.math.stonybrook.edu/pdf-Springer-final/016-0046.pdf))

The draft leaves implicit the object whose Čech cohomology is being taken; for a sharper stand-alone formulation, one should say that this is the first rational Čech cohomology of the corresponding tiling space. The paper elsewhere treats cohomology explicitly as a property of tiling spaces. ([armj.math.stonybrook.edu](https://armj.math.stonybrook.edu/pdf-Springer-final/016-0046.pdf))

The nearby discussion explains why this is the correct target rather than the irreducible-substitution-matrix version: Conjecture 2.2.2 is introduced because irreducibility of the characteristic polynomial of the abelianisation matrix M is not invariant under topological conjugacy, whereas spectral type is. ([armj.math.stonybrook.edu](https://armj.math.stonybrook.edu/pdf-Springer-final/016-0046.pdf))

If one wants the hypothesis 'unimodular' to be fully anchored in the paper's context, the neighboring text ties it to the abelianisation/substitution matrix M and notes that this assumption is often made so that λ is a unit in Z[λ]. ([armj.math.stonybrook.edu](https://armj.math.stonybrook.edu/pdf-Springer-final/016-0046.pdf))
refined_question: Is the Homological Pisot Conjecture true: for every one-dimensional unimodular Pisot inflation tiling T with expansion factor λ, where λ is a Pisot number, if the first rational Čech cohomology group of the corresponding tiling space has rank equal to the algebraic degree of λ, then must the associated tiling dynamical system have pure point dynamical spectrum?
justification: The draft is aiming at Conjecture 2.2.2, not Conjecture 2.2.1: the draft's cohomological hypothesis matches the statement of the Homological Pisot Conjecture exactly, whereas Conjecture 2.2.1 uses irreducibility of the characteristic polynomial of the abelianisation matrix M instead. The surrounding text in Section 2.2 explains that Conjecture 2.2.2 is introduced because irreducibility is not invariant under topological conjugacy, while spectral type is, and the immediately following Conjecture 2.2.3 is presented only as a later non-unimodular extension, not as an equivalent reformulation. I therefore kept the question narrowly at Conjecture 2.2.2 and sharpened only the implicit objects and terminology needed to make it stand alone: explicit universal quantification, the Pisot condition on λ, the tiling-space source of the Čech cohomology, and the dynamical meaning of 'pure point spectrum.' ([armj.math.stonybrook.edu](https://armj.math.stonybrook.edu/pdf-Springer-final/016-0046.pdf))
